A_PROOF.A_DEFINITION: A counts K4 quartets containing a triple support; each has at most one such support by pair-linearity, so A=sum_S |intersection N(v)|.
A_PROOF.E_DEFINITION: e is the number of triple supports containing both the unique degree-2 and unique degree-1 tickets; there is at most one.
A_PROOF.M_DEFINITION: m is the number of triple supports on all three degree-6 tickets; there is at most one such 3-set.
A_PROOF.PROOF: For each triple support S, a fourth common neighbour is outside S. For each v in S it is among at most g_v-2=4+d_v choices, so c(S)<=4+min_{v in S} d_v. Relative to 9 per support, a support through the unique d=2 ticket loses 3 (two supports total), a support through the unique d=1 ticket loses 4 (one total), their shared support restores 3, and the all-d=6 support adds 1. Therefore sum_S c(S)<=22*9-3*2-4+3e+m=188+3e+m. Since m,e are binary for every legal realization, m+3e<=4 and A<=192. This depends only on the full degree profile and frozen pair-linearity, not on a sampled realization.
